question.text: Natural glucose is termed D-glucose because :

options.text: $-\mathrm{OH}$ on the second carbon is on the right side in Fischer projection
$-\mathrm{OH}$ on the sixth carbon is on the right side in Fischer projection.
$-\mathrm{OH}$ on the fifth carbon is on the right side in Fischer projection.

solution.text: Fischer gave the prefix "D" to compounds whose bottom chiral has its $\mathrm{OH}$ to the right. So natural glucose is called D-glucose or dextrose. Structure of D-Glucose :
